name: Henry Art Gallery
funding: $4.8M. City of Seattle, 4Culture, Washington State Arts Commission and NEA; Frankenthaler and ArtsFund funds; sponsors include Phillips and Pyramid Breweries.
watch: Museum of the University of Washington in Seattle.
records_note: Annual reports from FY2015-16 to FY2024-25 are on its site, 990s are on ProPublica, a named funders page is undated, and trustees are listed.

name: How Art Museum
funding: Private museum of hotelier-collector Zheng Hao, opened 2017 beside his Onehome Art Hotel in Zhangjiang.
watch: Sister venue to his private museum in Wenzhou, opened 2013.
records_note: The museum's official site did not load (howartmuseum.org returned a gateway error), so nothing about its reports, accounts, funders or board could be checked.

name: iMAL
funding: Small art-and-tech centre (2025) with structural funding from Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, Flanders and VGC, plus the National Lottery and the ERDF.
watch: Canal-side centre and fablab in Molenbeek. Its private partners are Fondation Orange (telecom) and Selligent (software).
records_note: iMAL names its board and shows public and private partners as logos, but posts no annual reports or accounts.

name: Index - The Swedish Contemporary Art Foundation
funding: Swedish Arts Council, City of Stockholm, Region Stockholm. Non-profit foundation returns published annually.
watch: Began in 1974 as the underground photo magazine Bildtidningen. Index publishes critical theory, runs writing groups and shows conceptual work on art's role in society.

name: Institute of Modern Art
funding: Arts Queensland and Creative Australia. Partners include Sullivan+Strumpf, The Calile Hotel, Coopers, Bird in Hand, Autex and Creative Brisbane Collab.
watch: Oldest independent contemporary art center in Australia (Brisbane, est. 1975).
records_note: Names its board, shows funders and partners as undated logos, and links no annual reports or accounts from its site.

name: Instituto Tunga
funding: Artist's estate institute. The Tunga catalogue raisonné it leads is sponsored by Itaú and Sabesp under the Rouanet Law.
watch: The researcher's Itaú Cultural credit is wrong: the catalogue page names the bank Itaú and the state water utility Sabesp.
records_note: Its own site institutotunga.org showed a maintenance notice, so reports, accounts, funders and board were not checked.

name: Ishara Art Foundation
funding: Self-funded by founder Smita Prabhakar, who directs AMS International, a Dubai HR and events firm. Based at Alserkal Avenue; Abdelmonem Alserkal is honorary chairman of the trustees.
watch: The National (2024): 'completely self-funded'. A 2017 profile also lists her at Lazer Capital (infrastructure, oil and gas); no source links it to Ishara.
records_note: The site lists its trustees and advisory board; it publishes no annual reports, accounts or funders.

name: Jameel Arts Centre
funding: Privately funded by Art Jameel, the cultural arm of the Saudi group Abdul Latif Jameel. Not financed or run by the UAE state.
watch: Independent contemporary arts institution on Dubai Creek. Funded through the Jameel family philanthropic foundation; free public admission with emphasis on community learning and environmental research.
records_note: Neither the centre's site nor parent Art Jameel's site publishes annual reports, accounts, a funder list or a board.

name: Javett Art Centre at the University of Pretoria (Javett-UP)
funding: University of Pretoria gave the land and funding. The Javett Foundation funded construction and pledged ten years of annual gifts for running costs and an endowment.
watch: Opened September 2019. An independent trust runs it. Michael Javett founded the Unisec Group, later sold to Standard Bank, and Tolux, now Brait.
records_note: Posts one annual artistic report, for 2023, with no figures; no accounts, funder list or board names on its site.

name: Jim Thompson Art Center
funding: Run by the James H.W. Thompson Foundation, which says it relies entirely on its own funding.
watch: The foundation also supervises the Jim Thompson House Museum. The claim that house-museum income pays for the centre is not on its page.
records_note: The art centre publishes nothing itself; its parent foundation lists seven trustees, says it funds itself, and shows no reports, accounts or donors.

name: Julia Stoschek Foundation (Julia Stoschek Collection / JSC Berlin)
funding: Private Philanthropic Endowment (Julia Stoschek Foundation gGmbH).
watch: Autonomous non-profit foundation gGmbH with transparent public reporting and curatorial independence.

name: KALEKTAR research platform on Belarusian contemporary art
funding: German Federal Foreign Office (Civil Society Cooperation programme) and Rönne-Stiftung, per the platform's own about page
watch: Online archive, index and journal founded 2015; co-founder and editor-in-chief Sergey Shabohin lives and works in Białystok, which is used as the map point since the platform publishes no address.
records_note: Its About and Partners pages name funders, undated; the site posts no annual reports, accounts or board, only an editorial team and advisory council.
